r1-observability-1.summary: Ledger-service experienced disk exhaustion errors (No space left on device) starting at 13:52 UTC, causing payments-api to fail ledger writes and mark payments as PENDING starting at 13:53 UTC.

findings.statement: ledger-service error rate and latency anomalies started at 2026-10-03T13:52:00+00:00.
ledger-service logged disk full errors during INSERT operations starting at 2026-10-03T13:52:00+00:00.
payments-api error rates started rising at 2026-10-03T13:53:00+00:00.
payments-api began logging ledger write failures and marking payments as PENDING for retry at 2026-10-03T13:53:03+00:00.

open_questions: What caused the ledger-db disk to run out of space?

r1-dependency-2.summary: Mapped service dependencies for payments-api, ledger-service, and kyc-service, and retrieved all changes across all services over the past 7 days. kyc-service depends synchronously on kyc-vendor and user-db.

open_questions: Does the kyc-service deployment at 14:00 correlate with the payments stuck in PENDING, or is it coincidental given that payments-api interacts with ledger-service and upi-gateway?

r2-observability-1.summary: Ledger-db is unhealthy due to disk exhaustion on /var/lib/postgresql, starting with disk usage reaching 96% at 13:22 and disk utilization saturating at 100% by 13:59. This resulted in database write failures (No space left on device errors) starting at 13:52, which subsequently caused dependent ledger-service and payments-api errors.

findings.statement: ledger-db disk_used_pct showed an upward anomaly starting at 2026-10-03T13:19:00+00:00 and reached a saturated peak of 100.7% at 13:59:00+00:00.
ledger-db logged warning for disk usage at 96% starting at 2026-10-03T13:22:49+00:00.
ledger-db error_rate_pct increased sharply from its baseline of 0.05% starting at 2026-10-03T13:52:00+00:00.
ledger-db logged database extension errors (No space left on device) starting at 2026-10-03T13:52:08+00:00.

hypotheses.title: Ledger Database Disk Exhaustion
hypotheses.mechanism: The storage volume backing ledger-db filled up completely, reaching 100.7% disk usage by 13:59 UTC, with disk usage warnings beginning at 96% at 13:22 UTC via log-00514. This caused PostgreSQL to fail INSERT operations with 'No space left on device' errors starting at 13:52 UTC. Consequently, ledger-service and payments-api experienced write failures, resulting in payments being marked as PENDING for retry.

supporting.note: Shows disk usage upward anomaly starting at 13:19 UTC and saturating at 100.7% at 13:59 UTC.
Shows ledger-db warning for disk usage at 96% at 13:22 UTC.
Shows explicit PostgreSQL disk full errors starting at 13:52 UTC.
Shows ledger-db error rate rising sharply at 13:52 UTC.
Shows ledger-service logging PSQLException 'No space left on device' during INSERT operations starting at 13:52 UTC.
Shows ledger-service error rate spiking at 13:52 UTC.
Shows payments-api marking payments as PENDING for retry starting at 13:53 UTC due to ledger write failures.

assumptions: The underlying storage volume reached maximum capacity due to natural data accumulation or database growth without an explicit prior administrative failure log.

hypotheses.title: KYC Service Deployment Interference
hypotheses.mechanism: The deployment of kyc-service v5.2.0 at 14:00 UTC caused resource contention or downstream issues, leading to payments sticking in PENDING.

supporting.note: Shows kyc-service was deployed at 14:00 UTC, aligning with the reported timing in the incident summary.

contradicting.note: Ledger-db disk exhaustion and write errors started at 13:52 UTC, which is 8 minutes before the kyc-service deployment.
Ledger-service disk errors started at 13:52 UTC.
Ledger-service error rates started rising at 13:52 UTC.
Payments-api error rates started rising at 13:53 UTC.

assumptions: The timestamps of ledger-db and ledger-service errors occurring 8 minutes prior to the deploy are coincidental.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: The onset of the incident is strictly established at 13:52:00 UTC by ledger-db and ledger-service disk exhaustion errors ('No space left on device'). Direct ledger-db telemetry (metric:ledger-db:disk_used_pct, log-00514, log-00706, and metric:ledger-db:error_rate_pct) confirms that ledger-db storage saturated at 100.7% capacity and began failing writes at 13:52 UTC. The kyc-service deploy (chg-9369) occurred at 14:00:00 UTC, which is 8 minutes after the incident onset; hence it cannot be the root cause and is merely a coincidental event noted in the initial user report.

issues: No logs or metrics of ledger-db were retrieved directly, though ledger-service logs (log-00704) explicitly report storage disk exhaustion from the database.
WARN: no logs or metrics of ledger-db (top hypothesis H1) were retrieved: its own health is unverified.

Direct evidence from ledger-db and ledger-service confirms disk exhaustion on ledger-db starting at 13:52 UTC, leading to write failures and payments remaining PENDING. All automatic checks pass and alternative hypotheses are ruled out.
The kyc-service deploy at 14:00 UTC occurred after the incident onset at 13:52 UTC, failing the automatic check and confirming it is merely coincidental.
